 Stars Hollow is one of TV’s most idyllic small towns, but a new Gilmore Girls documentary, Drink Coffee, Talk Fast , reveals the set wasn’t always an ideal environment for cast and crew.
 While Alexis Bledel, who played Rory, didn’t participate in the documentary , Gilmore Girls alums recalled that, as a teenager, she struggled with long hours and late scripts.
 “She was just like 18 years old, and ‘I’m here for 60, 70 hours a week. What am I doing with my life?’ And it’s pretty, it’s gruelling,” Mark Strasburg, first assistant camera, said in a confessional interview. “It’s something you really had to want to do. There were definitely moments she knew she didn’t want to be there.”
 Chad Michael Murray, who played Rory’s classmate Tristin Dugray, also reflected on Bledel — who hadn’t had a typical high school experience due to traveling as a model — navigating the demanding role.
 “She had a big responsibility, because this is a girl who wasn’t accustomed to this industry,” the Gilmore Girls star recalled. She was so quiet. Well, it would make sense why she was so quiet. She was working every day, and a billion lines, and they’re gonna be spat out razor-sharp and fast.”

 While television shows typically had 45 to 50-page scripts, Gilmore Girls scripts were closer to 80 or 90 pages, which meant actors had to talk faster to avoid cuts. Creator Amy Sherman-Palladino also expected everyone to be “word perfect,” which was an especially difficult challenge when scripts were delivered late.
 Documentary participants recalled scripts arriving at 2:00 a.m. the day of a shoot or lengthy new scenes coming at 6:00 a.m. The unique way the series operated reportedly left Gilmore Girls cast and crew members exhausted. Bledel even fell asleep on camera once…
 “The only time in my 30-year career of directing that I’ve had an actor fall asleep on camera in the middle of a scene was Alexis Bledel,” director Jamie Babbit shared.
 “It had been like an 18-hour shooting day, a lot of dialogue, and there’s a shot that we want to show that Dean and Rory have fallen asleep,” Jared Padalecki recalled. “And we literally just fell asleep. I remember somebody shaking my arm, and I’m like, ‘Oh, sure. I’m ready.’ So in the scene, we’re fucking sleeping.”
 Photo: Richard Foreman / ©The CW /Courtesy Everett Collection 
 Archival footage featured in the documentary showed an old interview in which Scott Patterson said, “Alexis was really overwhelmed by being away from her family, maybe having some second thoughts about what she had gotten herself into. ‘Is this really a way to spend my youth?’ She was terribly homesick. And what was nice to see was the bond that formed off the set between Lauren and Alexis, because Lauren really helped her out.”
 After Sherman-Palladino departed the show after Season 6, production hours were significantly shaved, which was a relief to many, including Bledel.
 “The [Season 7] mandate was, ‘We don’t care if it’s good or not. We just want to go home,'” Babbit said. “When Alexis got the role, I don’t think she really realized that it was going to be six years of her life. I think she was pretty relieved to finally have a life.”
